# Jubilees Chapter 30 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Dinah and Shechem; the intermarriage ban; Simeon and Levi praised

---

**30:1** In the first year of the first week of the forty-fifth jubilee, Jacob came to Salem, the city of Shechem in the land of Canaan, after traveling from Paddan-aram, and he arrived there in peace.

**30:2** Shechem son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of the land, saw her and seized her and lay with her and violated her. She was a young girl, twelve years of age.

**30:3** He then pleaded with his father and with the brothers of Dinah that Dinah might be given to him as a wife.

**30:4** Jacob and his sons were furious over the violation of their sister Dinah, and they spoke to them with deception and acted treacherously toward them.

**30:5** Then Simeon and Levi fell upon the city without warning and killed every male. They recovered their sister Dinah and departed.

**30:6** Jacob was displeased with Simeon and Levi because they had acted in rage, and Jacob said: "You have made trouble for me, making me odious to the inhabitants of the land."

**30:7** But the LORD was not displeased with them, for they had acted with zeal for righteousness and had exacted vengeance on those who had violated their sister.

**30:8** There is no pardon for anyone who violates his neighbor's daughter, for it is an abomination before the LORD.

**30:9** Israel loved Dinah and was glad for what they had done, because they had defended the honor of Israel.

**30:10** Command the children of Israel that they shall not give their daughters to Gentiles, and that they shall not take Gentile daughters for their sons; for this is unclean and abominable before the LORD.

**30:11** Israel will not be clean from this defilement if he takes a wife from among the daughters of the Gentiles or gives his daughter to a son of the Gentiles.

**30:12** For it is a corruption and a destruction and a plague before the LORD.

**30:13** There shall be no pardon or forgiveness for the whole sin of this transgression forever; the man who has committed it shall die childless in the midst of the people, and he shall be cut off.

**30:14** For it is thus that I commanded Abraham, and Isaac, and his seed after him — that they should observe this statute and this ordinance and this law.

**30:15** This statute is ordained and inscribed on the heavenly tablets: there shall be no defilement through these abominations; everyone who commits them shall be cut off.

**30:16** All the descendants of the sons of Israel who defile themselves by giving their daughters to foreign peoples, or by taking foreign women — their descendants shall be rooted out from among their people.

**30:17** No abomination shall be committed in Israel; no Israelite shall defile himself with a foreign woman, for it is pollution and uncleanness.

**30:18** There will be no forgiveness for the sin of the nations who violate the daughters of Israel.

**30:19** Simeon and Levi are recorded as righteous in the heavenly tablets, for they acted with zeal and turned defilement away from Israel.

**30:20** Their names are written before the Holy One as righteous forever and ever, and they shall be praised forever, for they were zealous on behalf of their God.

**30:21** It is written in the heavenly tablets concerning Shechem and those who joined him: what they did was done to them in return for what they had done to the sons of Israel. And their names are inscribed in the heavenly tablets as destined for destruction in every generation.

**30:22** To Levi, God gave the priesthood — to him and his sons forever — because he was zealous to do justice and judgment and vengeance against all who rose up against Israel.

**30:23** Therefore the priesthood is given to Levi and his sons forever. They shall eat all the firstfruits before the LORD and be exalted; they shall receive the tithes of all Israel and the firstlings of everything — grain and wine and oil and cattle and sheep.

**30:24** Command the children of Israel: "Observe this word, for it is a statute for all time, inscribed on the heavenly tablets."

**30:25** And if a man violates the daughter of Israel, he shall be put to death; for it is written and decreed on the heavenly tablets: "Bring him out and put him to death; stone him, for he has defiled Israel."

---

*SOPHIA notes: Consensus following LOGOS base text. This is among the most significant chapters in Jubilees: the rehabilitation of Simeon and Levi, the inscription of the intermarriage ban in the heavenly tablets, and the grounding of the Levitical priesthood in Levi's zeal at Shechem. PNEUMA's contextual notes were valuable for understanding the theological stakes, but the formal register was maintained throughout per project standards.*
